newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa plans flights rejig - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans flights rejig - magazine.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday it planned to refocus its domestic and continental European flight structure, aimed at separating flights at the Frankfurt and Munich hubs from other flights.

The German magazine Manager said in a report released in advance of publication that Lufthansa wanted to start up a company offering cheaper flights on domestic and continental European flights not flying via Frankfurt and Munich.
The magazine quoted Deutsche Lufthansa board member Carl Sigel saying the airline planned to make a "clear distinction between flights on the Frankfurt and Munich hubs and decentralised air traffic".
Lufthansa chief operating officer Frederick Reid was quoted in the magazine saying that an low-price, low-cost airline product would be a good idea.
A Lufthansa spokeswoman said that the project was still in its infacy, a project manager was still being sought and that the start date had yet to be decided.
She said that finer details of the project contained in the report in the magazine were speculation.
The magazine said that the project proposed introducing a single-class system, reducing the range of in-flight refreshments and cutting back on seating room.

Employees would continue to be paid according to the usual company pay rulings, the magazine report said, and according to current planning structures the new project would be built up over a number of years.

The initial focus of the restructuring would be in Berlin, while in the long term around one third of aircraft set aside for domestic and continental European passage would be transferred to the new group, the magazine report said.
